Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `stable` @ `b728d0ac545fe1c418e8c92375a848b90e27e2be`. This matches the integration branch metadata (`stable`), so the branches agree.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends test_automation_grant_requires_trusted_author_and_exact_paths
Scope-mode justification: The clarification answer Q1 = B sets the scope: add a regression test and a changelog fragment, and change no logic. The verified heal-scope marker for this issue allows only `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, `tests/**` and `changelog.d/*.md`. The fix the issue proposes needs `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml`, `scripts/workflow_wrapper_refs.py` and `scripts/review_security_hold_sweep.py`, and the implement step would refuse all three as `out_of_heal_scope`. The guard that failed on bitsafe.io#498 worked correctly. `build_automation_grant` (`scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:177-209`) returns `no_allowlist` when a trusted author's issue body has no `files_touched:` block. `check_automation_paths` (lines 212-238) then denies every staged automation path with that reason, even with `allow_workflow_edits="true"`. So the useful deliverable here is to pin that exact behaviour so no later change can weaken it, and to record that the `ai-review.yml` sweep problem is deferred. A test that goes through both the function and the CLI costs about 25 lines more than a function-only test. Under the Boil the Lake rule (Correctness & safety ranks above Speed in §6), it is worth including.

## Automation / scheduling surface (§20.E)
- **New script, extended script, or code-only change:** none of these. This change only adds a test (in an existing test module) and one changelog fragment. No new scripts.
- **Scheduler / PR-push entry point:** none new. The test runs in the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` test jobs, which already collect `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py`. The fragment is folded in by the existing `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` run in `mark-stable.yml` / `test-and-mark-stable.yml`.
- **Long-running supervisor:** not needed.
- **DB work / gate pattern:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry:** none needed, because no script is added.

## Files likely to change
1. `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py`: add one new test function after `test_automation_grant_cli_denies_invalid_file_and_preserves_old_exit_codes` (ends at line 328), before the "Layer 2" banner at line 331.
2. `changelog.d/<this-issue-number>-heal-automation-guard-regression.md`: new file. The `changelog.d/` directory does not exist on this ref, so creating the file creates it. The implementer uses the GitHub issue number of this heal issue as the prefix.

Do not modify: `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, anything under `scripts/**`, anything under `workflow-templates/**`, or any guard logic.

## Functions / modules to implement
New test `test_automation_grant_denies_ungranted_wrapper_edit_bitsafe_498`. The name is unique: the module's existing `test_*` names were checked. Follow the style of the existing test at lines 279-307, using `guard`, `json`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `tempfile`, `Path` and `GUARD_SCRIPT`, all already imported or defined in the module.

Function-level cases:
- `staged = [".github/workflows/ai-review.yml"]`.
- `body` is a security-audit-style body with no `files_touched:` block, e.g. `"[security-audit] moving-ref-executed-with-pat\n\nworkflow-templates/ai-review.yml checks out stable and runs with GH_PAT.\n"`. Optional: also mention the path in prose to show that a prose mention grants nothing.
- Case A, pipeline-login author: `meta = {"number": 498, "user": {"login": "pipeline[bot]"}, "author_association": "NONE", "body": body}`.
  - `grant = guard.build_automation_grant(meta, "pipeline[bot]")`
  - Assert `grant["trusted"] is False`, `grant["reason"] == "no_allowlist"` and `grant["paths"] == []`.
  - Assert `guard.check_automation_paths(staged, grant, "true", "498") == ("out-of-scope", [".github/workflows/ai-review.yml"], "no_allowlist")`.
- Case B, OWNER author: same as A with `user.login="maintainer"` and `author_association="OWNER"`, and the same two assertions.
- No-bypass check: `allow_workflow_edits="true"` is the most permissive input and still denies (covered above). Also assert `check_automation_paths(staged, grant, "false", "498")[2] == "workflow_edits_disabled"`, which still reports `out-of-scope`.
- Mixed staging: `check_automation_paths(staged + ["tests/x.py", "changelog.d/1-x.md"], grant, "true", "498")` returns `("out-of-scope", [".github/workflows/ai-review.yml"], "no_allowlist")`. Non-automation paths never appear in the denied list.
- Case variant: `".GitHub/workflows/ai-review.yml"` is still detected as an automation path and denied, since `is_automation_path` lower-cases the first segment.

CLI case, in a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`, mirroring lines 310-328:
- Write `meta.json` with case B and `staged.txt` containing `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml\n`.
- Run `[sys.executable, str(GUARD_SCRIPT), "--emit-automation-grant", grant_file, "--issue-meta-file", meta, "--pipeline-login", "pipeline[bot]"]`. Expect return code 0, and the parsed grant JSON has `reason == "no_allowlist"`.
- Run `--check-automation-paths --automation-grant-file <grant> --staged-file <staged> --allow-workflow-edits true --issue-number 498`. Expect `returncode == 30`, `stdout.strip() == ".github/workflows/ai-review.yml"` and `stderr.splitlines()[0] == "reason=no_allowlist"`. These come from `main()` lines 383-388 and `EXIT_AUTOMATION_UNGRANTED = 30`.
- Add a short comment naming the incident: bitsafe.io#498, implement run 38125381156, step "Preflight destructive-commit guard".

## Data structures affected
None. The test only reads the existing grant record shape (`schema_version`, `issue_number`, `trusted`, `reason`, `author_login`, `author_association`, `paths`).

## API or interface changes
None. No CLI flags, exit codes, log keys or env vars change.

## Decisions
### D1 — Regression test plus changelog fragment instead of the template fix
- **Chosen:** Pin the automation-path guard's `no_allowlist` denial for an ungranted workflow-wrapper edit, and record the deferral in a changelog fragment.
- **Alternatives considered:** Change `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml`, `scripts/workflow_wrapper_refs.py` and `scripts/review_security_hold_sweep.py` here (the issue's suggested fix). Or close the issue with no change.
- **Why:** The clarification answer Q1 = B is binding. The verified heal scope excludes those files, and widening it would fail `implement_heal_preflight.sh`'s marker verification. A test protects the guard that behaved correctly, which follows the constraint "do not weaken the failing guard". Closing with no change would leave that behaviour unprotected.

### D2 — Cover both the Python functions and the CLI
- **Chosen:** Assert through `build_automation_grant`/`check_automation_paths` and through the `--emit-automation-grant` / `--check-automation-paths` CLI.
- **Alternatives considered:** A function-only test.
- **Why:** `implement.yml` calls the CLI, and exit code 30 plus `reason=no_allowlist` on stderr is what the workflow reads. The extra cost is about 15 lines.

### D3 — Ignore Q2 in this issue
- **Chosen:** No token or identity changes.
- **Alternatives considered:** Applying Q2 option A partially.
- **Why:** The Q2 answer itself says it does not apply when Q1 = B. It is guidance for a separate follow-up issue only.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundaries touched:** none at runtime. The test checks the existing boundary: an issue body from a trusted author still grants nothing for automation paths unless it has an exact `files_touched:` block. A prose mention of `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml` grants nothing.
- **Authorization:** no new endpoints or surfaces. The test confirms `allow_workflow_edits="true"` is necessary but not sufficient, so there is no bypass.
- **External input validation:** the fixture body is test-local data. The guard's parsing does not change.
- **Abuse cases this test pins:**
  - A consumer or heal issue tries to edit an upstream-managed wrapper by naming it only in prose. Denied with `no_allowlist`.
  - Mixing non-automation paths into the staged set does not hide the automation path.
  - A path-case variant (`.GitHub/...`) does not evade detection.
- **Known open weakness, deliberately out of scope:** `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml`'s security-hold sweep checks out a moving `stable` ref and runs with `secrets.GH_PAT || github.token`. It stays exploitable until the follow-up issue lands. The changelog fragment states this and does not claim it is fixed.
- No secrets go into fixtures. Logins are synthetic (`pipeline[bot]`, `maintainer`).

## Changelog fragment content
- First line: `<!-- changelog: fixed -->`. Arguably this is test coverage; `fixed` is used because it records the heal outcome. `changed` is also acceptable.
- Body, following the template in `docs/changelog-style.md`:
  - **Headline:** a regression test now pins the implement automation-path grant guard's denial of an ungranted `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml` edit (`reason=no_allowlist`, exit 30), from bitsafe.io#498 / run 38125381156.
  - **Lead:** the guard worked as designed. Upstream-managed wrappers are fixed in coding-workflows and delivered by `ai-update-workflows.yml`, not edited in consumers.
  - **"For contributors" subsection:** the security-hold sweep in `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` (moving `stable` checkout with `GH_PAT`) is not fixed here and is tracked in a separate follow-up.
- No invented numbers. Do not mention a follow-up issue number unless it exists. Avoid the vocabulary banned by the style guide.
